CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 56-year-old female with past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc presenting for annual examination. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. Carpal tunnel symptoms have resolved following prior surgical release, with full range of motion and no numbness or tingling in hands. She is back to work without issues. Over the last month, she has been experiencing chest pain that occurs with walking and resolves with rest. She does not have chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest, occurring approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She reports some nasal congestion from allergies related to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses chest pain with exertion that resolves with rest. She endorses nasal congestion from allergies. She denies shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, or fever and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently working.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation normal. Heart: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Carotid: No bruits appreciated. Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars noted on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from last year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45% (slightly low). Mitral regurgitation present (leaky heart valve).
EKG: Stable, reflects prior coronary artery disease, no new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release: No further intervention needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
2. Herniated disc: No further steroid injection or physical therapy needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Continue aspirin and Toprol. Order cardiac stress test. Order lipid panel. Start Crestor 20 mg once daily.
